key_insight: Variational quantum classifiers showed an expressivity–stability trade-off in network anomaly detection, but classical models performed better on the synthetic data.
engineering_relevance: Feature encoding, circuit architecture, and optimizer selection matter for quantum anomaly detectors, while classical methods remain the stronger baseline for this task.
method: Evaluated four VQC architectures with different encodings, ansatz circuits, quantum neural network types, and optimizers.
Compared VQCs against Support Vector Machine and Random Forest models.
evidence_signal: VQC-4 reached up to 89.0% accuracy, VQC-3 was identified as best overall using ZFeatureMap, RealAmplitudes, and ADAM, and classical baselines achieved perfect classification on the synthetic data.
watch_item: Synthetic data with relatively simple class separations does not establish real-world effectiveness or quantum advantage on noisy, high-dimensional traffic.
paper_title: Quantum Anomaly Detection in network traffic using Variational Quantum Classifiers
